scope: Theorem 6.5 (Scalar comparison and admissibility) of the manuscript “Finite generation for the K(n)-local sphere” (preprints/Finite-generation-for-the-Kn-local-sphere-September-24-2026/Finite-generation-for-the-Kn-local-sphere-September-24-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 313 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 07b43c6077268638), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 48. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every s ≥ 0 and every compact profinite D, extension of constants induces natural quasi-isomorphisms ED ⊗Fp RΓc(Ys, Fp) ∼ − − → RΓc(Ys × D, Fp), (6.11) RD ⊗Fp RΓc(Ys, Fp) ∼ − − → RΓc(Ys × D, O♭ ). (6.12) The tensors are algebraic. The comparisons retain uniform support and all compact bar parameters. Each Hi c(Ys, Fp) is a countable smooth admissible Ms-module. It has a smooth commuting Pm-action. Smooth means that each vector has open stabilizer; admissible means that every open subgroup of Ms has finite-dimensional fixed space.
